verdict.rationale: Zapier documents centrally stored app connections that it reuses across surfaces, and mentions "managed connections" and "workspace controls" with permissions you control. However, the evidence never explicitly shows sharing a specific credential with teammates or per-credential access control; MCP server view/edit sharing is a different feature and earns no credit here. missing for 10: documented team sharing of individual connections, per-credential usage permissions (who can use which credential), in-depth first-party docs on connection governance, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an ops user, I can store connection credentials centrally, share them with my team, and control who can use which credential

citations.quote: Zapier brings in your existing app connections automatically.
Account-level restrictions, managed connections, and workspace controls apply to all of them.
all with managed auth and permissions you control
Zapier handles OAuth, credentials, and API complexity so you never touch a token.
